ARCHITECT VERDICT: r5 is feasible as ONE elevated sitting of about 53 min on the critical path (17 attended for the six Google consents, plus about 4 min for each conditional Claude/Codex re-login). That is about 3 min over the 50-min target. A fix-proof tail of about 15 min follows; it is unattended and needs no elevation. There is also a deterministic Gemini-held degrade mode of about 26 min.

What makes one sitting possible:
(a) The step-10 source accepts BOTH model_bindings forms (plain slug, or {argv, reports}), so no source change depends on tomorrow's receipts.
(b) The r5 config is produced in the sitting by a gated, deterministic builder. If any Gemini gate fails, the candidate is the commissioned file byte for byte (sha 135cd9ec, verified on disk at C:\Program Files\CoChem\Pipeline4.2.7-windows-20261009-r4\pipeline.json; gemini is held there by integration_hold). No non-Gemini fix needs any config field.
(c) Two pins cannot be pre-embedded and are bound by content verification inside the sitting: the r5 install-after.json sha and the staged-config sha.

Gaps in the manifest that this plan closes:
1. The custom agent is staged only in slot1 (isolation-evidence spec part a), while the production argv passes --agent cochem-inference-only on all six slots. Slots 2-6 would fail every Gemini job as 'protocol' or 'code', which poison-pills chapters. Six-slot agent staging plus a listing check is added as a Gemini gate.
2. A5's isolation_verdict has model_fallback_basis 'UNKNOWN', yet inference_only.disables_model_fallback must be literally true (inference_policy.py:130-132). The builder therefore needs an explicit rule: under 3B the basis is the identity policy plus the reroute scan plus a passing replay. Without this rule Gemini is always held.
3. Step 10's load_config rule 'every gemini target needs a binding' contradicts its own 'effort-null only' fallback. Resolved: no orphan bindings, at least one binding; unbound targets fail closed as 'compatibility' before any launch, which is the same spill behaviour as today's integration hold.
4. Rollback after r5 has started needs a stop that accepts the r5 action. retarget requires 0 instances and a pinned source action (retarget-warden-r4.ps1:184-190). So stop-warden-r5 is added, and retarget-warden-r5 must accept the r5 action as a source.
5. Agy identity, reroute or tool-registry violations are classified 'compatibility' (model hold plus reroute), not 'protocol' (failure_count poison pill).
6. Per-file line endings: the repo is LF while r4 is CRLF for coding.py, controller_guard.py and failures.py; most other files are mixed; agy_protocol.py is pure LF. The r4 freeze rule (freeze-stopped-runtime-r4-source.py:57-63) refuses a convention change and mixed line endings. Each r5 file must be committed in r4's convention, normalised to pure.
7. A5 evidences only the 'gemini-3.8-flash-high' slug. The effort-null binding needs an extra A5 run for the owner's slug, otherwise it binds the -high slug. The pro tier (7-9) stays unbound.

Changed-file list: 12 src files; verified_unchanged = 154 of 166.

(r4 root copy), agy.exe 38f30c7d...; root C:\Program Files\CoChem\InteractiveAgy427-r4-<slot>-<nonce>; task CoChem-4.2.7-InteractiveAgy-r4-<slot>-<nonce>, SYSTEM/BA SDDL, PT15M, action '-I -B <root>\worker_agy_login_bridge_r4_v1.py --slot <slot> --nonce <nonce>'; console loop identical to v6 (Test-InstanceComplete, 14-minute deadline, masked SecureString prompt from claude-code-input-v6.ps1 imported by hash, Enter submits, Escape cancels, Write-PrivatePacket CreateNew SYSTEM/BA, Clear-ClaudeConsoleInput boolean proof) with $nativePrompt='Or, paste the authorization code here and press Enter:' and a split-prefix guard; everything before the prompt (the sign-in URL) is written to the console; owner instruction text names Google sign-in. Receipt acceptance: schema cochem-interactive-agy-login/1, nonce/slot, system_sid S-1-5-18, helper sha, runtime bindings r4 (629c87ec/1202b1d7/38a99c3f/de7fac91/135cd9ec), cleanup_verified true, task LastTaskResult 0, status in {LOGIN_COMMAND_EXITED_ZERO_STATUS_REQUIRED, LOGIN_SESSION_ENDED_AFTER_INPUT_STATUS_REQUIRED}; result schema cochem-interactive-agy-login-result/1 with authentication_verified false and next_step 'reviewed native status check'. Bridge: constants INSTALL r4, NATIVE agy.exe, SUPPORT_SHA256 (six-r4-v1 module), MAX_INPUT 2048, MAX_OUTPUT 131072, LOGIN_SECONDS 600, POST_INPUT_SECONDS 120; run(): require_system, root/helper custody, support.validate_interpreter, windows.py hash ca07b3bb, support.verify_r4_runtime, support.require_stopped (four names), layout/config hashes, SID check, agy hash == CONTRACTS['gemini']['sha256'], limits from config execution_limits, argv [str(NATIVE)] (bare; no --login exists), launch_worker with stdin pipe and stdout/stderr pipe (never login_worker/gemini_login_argv), observe_child, run_loop as Claude (publish to operator.log until input.once, feed one line + '\n' then EOF, cancel.request -> InterruptedError). New after-input behaviour: wait up to POST_INPUT_SECONDS for exit; if agy exits 0 -> LOGIN_COMMAND_EXITED_ZERO_STATUS_REQUIRED; if it is still running (interactive TUI after sign-in) -> process.terminate() through the owned Job, record native_exit_code and terminated_after_input true, status LOGIN_SESSION_ENDED_AFTER_INPUT_STATUS_REQUIRED (the after-status check is the authority); non-zero exit before input -> LOGIN_COMMAND_FAILED with the sanitized phase (e.g. the documented 'authentication required' headless exit). Receipt adds native_output_bytes_before_input, prompt_seen_by_bridge false (bridge does not parse), one_line_submitted, input_file_deleted, operator_cancelled, login_commands_executed 1, model_jobs_executed 0. agy-session-history-r4-v1.ps1: Assert-ReviewedAgyHistory parameterised copy of Assert-ReviewedClaudeHistory with root filter InteractiveAgy427-r4-<slot>-*, task prefix CoChem-4.2.7-InteractiveAgy-r4-<slot>-, r4 layout path, bridge/support pins, receipt schema cochem-interactive-agy-login/1 and the two accepted terminal statuses; the 'older non-r3 session' guard becomes 'any InteractiveAgy427-<slot>-* root without -r4-'. Timeouts: task PT15M, wrapper 14 min, bridge 600 s pre-input + 120 s post-input, 30 s status checks. Cancel path: Escape -> cancel.request packet -> bridge InterruptedError -> cleanup terminates the Job, unloads the profile, deletes consumed packets by handle, receipt LOGIN_FAILED_OR_CANCELLED; the wrapper throws, the series throws (no later slot), the next attempt must pass Assert-ReviewedAgyHistory.

deployment_designs.open_risks: Largest unknown of the program: whether bare agy in a non-TTY session-0 process prints the sign-in URL and reaches the paste prompt at all (docs describe the paste path for remote terminals; binary strings exist). The discovery capture (A2 probe P6) answers it before any login; if it fails the sitting stops with evidence and there is no login path with this CLI version. Whether the token lands in Credential Manager or in .gemini\antigravity-cli\antigravity-oauth-token under the worker profile is UNKNOWN; either is inside the worker's own profile and is observed by the after-status. Terminating a TUI after sign-in could in principle interrupt token persistence; mitigated by the 120 s grace and the after-status gate. Replacing worker-native-status-r3.py by the six-r4-v1 module as the bridge's support is a simplification that review must accept (worker-native-status-r3.py was not read in this design).

cli_designs.component: (b) Login start for the per-slot bridge (worker_agy_login_bridge_r4.py)
cli_designs.purpose: Start Antigravity's Google-account sign-in inside the worker's token/profile, surface the authorization URL to the owner's console, deliver the one-line authorization code, and exit zero so the after-status (component a) can prove the session.
cli_designs.interface: Bridge shape = the Claude r3 bridge (launch_worker(identity, argv, cwd=slot root, stdin=pipe, stdout/stderr=pipe, limits), pump output to <root>\operator.log until the packet is submitted, feed exactly one line, stop publishing, wait for exit, verify Job cleanup/UnloadUserProfile) with these agy specifics. Discovery order for the slot1 attended run (stop at the first that works): B1 argv [agy.exe, "-p", "/model"] -- print mode with a read-only slash command (no inference; v1.1.11 '/model emits one tab-separated record'), prompt supplied in argv so stdin is free for the code; expected success transcript: 'Starting OAuth authentication flow' / 'Please visit the following URL to authorize the application:' or 'Authentication required. Please visit the URL to log in:' followed by a line beginning 'https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth' (redirect expected to be https://antigravity.google/oauth-callback, which displays the code), then a code prompt ('Or, paste the authorization code here and press Enter:' | 'Enter the authorization code:' | 'Paste the authorization code below:'), then after the fed line 'Successfully exchanged authorization code for token' / 'Successfully authenticated as %s.' / 'Print mode: authenticated as %s', then the /model record 'gemini-...\tGemini ...' and exit 0. Expected failure transcript (then B1 is dead on this build): 'Print mode: not logged in and no controlling terminal; cannot complete interactive login' and/or 'Error: authentication required. Run 'agy' to log in.' with non-zero exit. B1' = same with ["--output-format","json","-p","/model"] (envelope on stdout; prompts probably on stderr). B2 (lowest likelihood, run only if B1 fails and only once): bare [agy.exe] -- documented sign-in entry but a bubbletea TUI needing a console ('closing CONIN$', 'bubbletea: error restoring console') and a 'Select login method:' picker; expect immediate failure under CREATE_NO_WINDOW. B3/B4 (require the r5 source change the owner already accepted under 3B, so they belong to the Phase-A contingency): B3 give the login child a console -- launch_worker(login=True) omits CREATE_NO_WINDOW and the bridge calls AllocConsole before launch so the child inherits it and agy's CONIN$ path (v1.1.2) works; the bridge delivers the code with WriteConsoleInputW(code + Enter) instead of the stdin pipe; B4 allow a fixed login-only env allowlist in _worker_environment ({'AGY_CLI_INTERACTIVE_HEADLESS':'1'} and always {'AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE':'true'}); AGY_CLI_CDE_AUTH_ACTION=login is a last candidate (binary: supported values check, login; apparent server-polled flow 'Authentication required. Please visit the URL to log in:' + 'Waiting for authentication (timeout 60s)...' with no code paste) and AGY_CLI_CDE_AUTH_ACTION=check the ideal probe if it prints status and exits -- both undocumented, not exercised in this task, owner-authorized discovery only. Bridge matching rules: publish operator.log lines until a line matches the code-prompt regex (?i)(paste|enter) the authorization code|Enter the redirect URL; highlight the first line matching ^https://; treat 'authenticated as ' lines as secret-bearing (account email) and never copy them into receipts; success = exit 0 AND a success marker seen; failure markers: 'authentication required', 'no controlling terminal', 'authentication interrupted', 'auth timed out', 'authorization code cannot be empty', 'no authorization code received', 'Error: authentication failed'. Deadline 15 min task limit as for Claude; the owner should open the URL immediately because 'Waiting for authentication (timeout 60s)...' may bound the consent window. Token lands in the worker's Credential Manager entry 'jetski-standalone-oauth-token' or, on keyring fallback, in C:\Users\CoChem422WorkerN\.gemini\antigravity-cli\antigravity-oauth-token; the receipt records which (existence/size only, never contents). Do NOT use cochem_pipeline.windows login --provider gemini / login_gemini_worker for the paste path: it feeds stdin from an empty temp file (cochem_supervisor/windows.py:890) so no code can be delivered; a contract JSON {provider:'gemini', executable, arguments:['-p','/model'], purpose:'subscription-login', capability_reference} satisfies gemini_login_argv (1..32 args) and could serve the B4 CDE/polled flow if it needs no stdin, but still cannot pass the env var.

cli_designs.tests: (1) Preview/dry run with the all-zero attempt (unelevated reports slot roots inaccessible). (2) Bridge unit tests with a fake child that emits each transcript variant (URL + prompt + success; 'no controlling terminal' failure; timeout) asserting publish-stop before the feed, no secret line in receipt.json, exit classification, and cleanup. (3) Owner slot1 discovery (SYSTEM task, 15 min cap): capture full operator.log (SYSTEM/BA-only), the exact prompt phrases and URL prefix seen, elapsed time from URL to success, whether a token file appeared under the worker's .gemini\antigravity-cli, and Credential Manager presence via a SYSTEM-side CredEnumerate under the worker token (names only). (4) Immediately run component (a) AFTER and require pass. (5) Repeat for slots 2-6 only after slot1 passes; the series must keep daemons stopped (2B) and one slot at a time.
cli_designs.open_risks: Highest-uncertainty item of the program: the CONIN$-based paste path plus CREATE_NO_WINDOW makes B1 likely to fail fast; then only source changes (B3 console/ConPTY or B4 env allowlist) or the undocumented CDE action remain, each needing review and a new runtime before any login can succeed. The 60 s wait string may cap the consent window below the 51-67 s per-slot Claude timings. The flow may require 'Select login method:' interaction (business/WIF/ADC) rather than the personal path. A loopback callback listener ('http://localhost:%d/auth/callback') may be opened in session 0 (harmless but should be recorded). Six consents from one Google account within minutes may be rate-limited (UNKNOWN). The owner's own earlier file-based fallback (antigravity-oauth-token in the owner profile) suggests keyring timeouts occur on this host; a worker hitting the same fallback stores the token in a plaintext-permission file inside the worker profile (SYSTEM/worker ACL) -- acceptable only if cleanup never deletes .gemini\antigravity-cli.
